bib.title: Scaling up GANs for Text-to-Image Synthesis
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv:2303.05511v2, cs.CV, 19 Jun 2023); ledger/references list CVPR 2023

read.skipped: Reference list entries [25]-[88] (about 11k chars) only skimmed for lineage; all body, tables and appendices read.

question: Can GANs be scaled up to large web-scale datasets such as LAION for text-to-image synthesis, as diffusion and autoregressive models have been?
hypothesis: Naive StyleGAN scaling is limited because the same convolution filters must model all text conditions at all locations; dynamic filter selection plus attention, multi-scale training and auxiliary losses should make GAN scaling stable.
contributions: First GAN-based method to train a billion-scale (1.0B) model on billions of real-world Internet images
Sample-adaptive kernel selection, interleaved L2 self-attention and cross-attention, multi-scale input/output discriminator with matching-aware loss, CLIP and vision-aided losses
Text-conditioned GAN upsampler usable as a drop-in super-resolution stage, up to 4K / 16 Mpix
Latent-space editing (style mixing, prompt interpolation, prompt mixing) retained at scale

method.summary: GigaGAN extends conditional StyleGAN2 with a bank of N filters selected per sample from the style vector, L2-distance self-attention and cross-attention interleaved with convolutions, and a multi-scale input/multi-scale output discriminator with matching-aware, CLIP contrastive and vision-aided losses. A 652.5M base generator makes 64px images and a 359.1M upsampler makes 512px; the pair is 1.0B parameters and evaluated zero-shot on COCO.
method.task: text-to-image synthesis (also ImageNet class-conditional and super-resolution)

datasets.name: LAION2B-en + COYO-700M
datasets.size: null (total images seen: 0.98B for GigaGAN in Table 2)
datasets.preprocessing: center crop to square, resize to 64x64 with PIL.LANCZOS; filter pairs by image resolution (>=512), CLIP score (>0.3), aesthetics score (>5.0); watermarked images removed

datasets.name: Adobe internal Stock images
datasets.source: Adobe internal; used only for the 128-to-1024 upsampler

datasets.name: ImageNet
datasets.preprocessing: center crop, resize to 64 or 256 with PIL.LANCZOS; FID uses 50k generated images vs entire training set

datasets.name: COCO2014 validation
datasets.preprocessing: center crop, resize to 299x299 with PIL.BICUBIC, clean-fid library

models.name: GigaGAN (text-to-image, base + upsampler)
models.architecture: StyleGAN2-derived GAN with adaptive kernel selection, self+cross attention, MS-I/O discriminator
models.tokenizer: CLIP tokenizer, prompt padded to C=77

other.upsampler_output: 512px; asymmetric U-Net with 3 downsampling and 6 upsampling residual blocks
other.text_encoder: frozen CLIP ViT-L/14, penultimate layer features, plus learned attention layers T (4 layers base, 2 layers upsampler)

models.name: Stable Diffusion v1.5, LDM, Imagen, Parti, DALL-E 2, GLIDE, eDiff-I, Muse, LAFITE, SD-distilled, Real-ESRGAN, SD Upscaler, SR3

training.objective: V = V_MS-I/O (non-saturating GAN loss + matching-aware loss) + L_CLIP (contrastive) + L_Vision (vision-aided GAN); upsampler also LPIPS loss, no vision-aided loss; style mixing and path length regularisation turned off
training.lr: 0.0025 for G and D (all tasks, Table A2)
training.batch_size: text-to-image base 512~1024; text-to-image upsampler 192~320; ablation rows 256 (100k steps)
training.steps: 1350k iterations (base text-to-image); 915k (64->512 upsampler); 160k (ImageNet SR); 300k and 620k (ImageNet 64 and 64->256)
training.regularisation: R1 strength 0.2048 ~ 2.048 (base), interval 16; matching loss strength 1.0 (G and D); CLIP loss strength 0.2 ~ 1.0 (base), 1.0 (upsampler); LPIPS strength 10.0 (upsampler); G EMA beta 0.9999 (base), 0.9890 (upsampler); Gaussian noise augmentation on upsampler
training.compute: GigaGAN 4,783 A100 GPU days; SD-v1.5 6,250 A100 GPU days; Imagen about 4,755 TPUv4 days; Parti about 320 TPUv4 days

other.ablation_protocol: all ablated models trained 100k steps, batch 256, except Scale-up row (1350k iterations, larger batch)

inference.decoding: single forward pass; optional text-conditioned truncation trick
inference.samples: 30,000 generated images for COCO FID-30k; 50k for ImageNet; w_mean,c averaged over 16 samples of M(z,c)
inference.prompting: text prompt padded to 77 tokens; no prompt engineering described

parameters.truncation_psi: 1.0 = none; paper finds 0.7 to 0.8 best visually; Fig A3 sweeps [1.0, 0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5]
parameters.truncation_formula: w_trunc = lerp(w_mean,c, lerp(w_mean, w, psi), psi)
parameters.timing_hardware: null (inference-time hardware not stated; training and evaluation on A100)

other.diffusion_baseline_settings: SD-v1.5 50 steps, guidance 7.5, 512px, 2.9s; LDM 250 steps, guidance 6.0, 256px, 9.4s (Fig A9)
other.output_resize: GigaGAN 512px images resized to 256px before FID in Table 2

metrics.name: FID
metrics.definition: Frechet Inception Distance, clean-fid library, bicubic resize to 299x299; FID-10k/30k/5k/50k denote number of generated images

metrics.name: CLIP score
metrics.definition: image-text alignment; ViT-B/32 in Table 1, OpenCLIP ViT-G/14 elsewhere

metrics.name: patch-FID, LPIPS, IS, PSNR, SSIM, Precision/Recall

eval.protocol: No seeds, repeats or significance tests reported. Paper concedes large differences in training data, text encoders, iterations, batch size and model size across baselines; most baseline numbers are taken from papers except SD-v1.5 evaluated by the authors.

availability.code: null (website mentioned, no URL stated in text)
availability.data: LAION2B-en and COYO-700M public; Adobe Stock internal

evidence.quote: GigaGAN initially synthesizes 512px images, which are resized to 256px before evaluation.
All ablated models are trained for 100k steps at a batch size of 256 except for the Scale-up row (1350k iterations with a larger batch size).

results.claim: GigaGAN reaches zero-shot COCO FID-30k of 9.09, lower than SD-v1.5 (9.62, evaluated by the authors), DALL-E 2 (10.39) and Parti-750M (10.71), at 0.13s per 512px image.
results.setup: COCO2014 validation, zero-shot; 512px output resized to 256px before FID; 1.0B GigaGAN; baselines differ in data, encoders and resolution
results.quote: GigaGAN achieves a zero-shot FID of 9.09 on COCO2014 dataset, lower than the FID of DALL·E 2, Parti-750M, and Stable Diffusion.

results.claim: GigaGAN inference time is 0.13s for a 512px image versus 2.9s for SD-v1.5.
results.setup: 512px output; Table 2; inference hardware not stated
results.table: Table 2, row GigaGAN, column Inf. time
results.note: Table 2 prints 0.13s for GigaGAN and 2.9s for SD-v1.5*

results.claim: Naively making the StyleGAN2 baseline 5.7x larger worsens FID (29.91 to 34.07) in the 64px ablation.
results.setup: 64px text-to-image, 100k steps, batch 256; StyleGAN2 27.8M vs Larger 158.9M

results.claim: Ablation adds components one by one and FID-10k falls from 29.91 (StyleGAN2) to 9.18 for the scaled-up 652.5M model.
results.setup: 64px base; Scale-up row trained 1350k iterations with larger batch, others 100k steps batch 256
results.note: Matching-aware D alone worsens FID (23.87 to 27.29) but raises CLIP score; multi-scale training leaves FID flat (14.88 to 14.92) while CLIP score rises 0.280 to 0.300

results.claim: Against progressively distilled SD, GigaGAN has better FID-5k (21.1 vs 26.0 best of 2/4/8/16 steps) and CLIP 0.32, in one step.
results.setup: COCO2017, 512px resize, SD-distilled protocol; GigaGAN 1 step 0.13s vs SD-distilled-4 0.33s
results.quote: Table 3 demonstrates that GigaGAN remains faster than the distilled Stable Diffusion while showing better FID and CLIP scores of 21.1 and 0.32, respectively.

results.claim: GigaGAN text-conditioned 128->1024 upsampler has FID-10k 1.54 vs 8.60 Real-ESRGAN and 9.39 SD Upscaler, at 0.13s.
On ImageNet 64->256 unconditional super-resolution GigaGAN gets FID-50k 1.2 with one step, vs 5.2 for SR3 (100 steps) and 2.4 for LDM-4.
results.setup: ImageNet 64->256, GigaGAN 359M; PSNR 24.3 is lower than U-Net regression 27.9

results.claim: Class-conditional ImageNet 256px: GigaGAN FID 3.45 (569M), worse than StyleGAN-XL 2.32 (166M) and DiT-XL/2 2.27.
results.setup: ImageNet 256px, no pretrained classifier, base 64px model plus 256px upsampler end-to-end finetuned
results.table: Table A1, row GigaGAN, column FID
results.note: Authors say StyleGAN-XL has lowest FID but visually worse

results.claim: GigaGAN is 36x larger than StyleGAN2 and 6x larger than StyleGAN-XL and XMC-GAN.
results.note: Text truncated across line break at page 1 to 2: '36x larger than Style-GAN2 and 6x larger than StyleGAN-XL and XMC-GAN'

results.claim: Authors concede visual quality is not yet comparable to production-grade models like DALL-E 2 in photorealism and text alignment.
results.setup: Fig 9 and Appendix C failure cases
results.quote: However, the visual quality of our results is not yet comparable to production-grade models like DALL·E 2.

results.claim: Authors say lower FID does not mean better images and zero-shot COCO FID may be a corner case.
results.quote: We acknowledge that this may represent a corner case of zero-shot FID on COCO2014 dataset

results.claim: Truncation (psi 0.7 to 0.8) trades diversity for CLIP score, similar to guidance in diffusion models.
results.setup: Fig A3/A4, COCO FID-10k vs CLIP ViT-G/14; values read only from figure
results.quote: We find that a truncation value between 0.8 and 0.7 produces the best result.

limits: Authors concede quality below DALL-E 2 in photorealism, compositionality and structural coherency (Fig 9, A9-A14)
Comparison to baselines is uncontrolled: different datasets, text encoders, iterations, batch size, model size and resolution; only SD-v1.5 was evaluated by the authors
FID on COCO may be a corner case and does not track visual quality (authors)
Prompt-based style transfer works only for single, simple objects (Fig A7 caption)
No seeds, error bars or significance tests; no learning-rate schedule, warmup or training tokens stated; inference-timing hardware not stated; code and weights not stated
Model scale 1.0B is below Imagen 3.0B, DALL-E 2 5.5B, Parti 20B; 'no quality saturation yet observed' is asserted, not shown beyond Table 1
Authors expect improvement with larger models; the claim 'conclusive answer about the scalability of GANs' rests on one 1B model

terms.definition: A bank of N filters is instantiated and the style vector w predicts softmax weights to average them into one filter per sample (Eq. 1)
multi-scale input, multi-scale output discriminator in which each pyramid level makes real/fake predictions at all subsequent scales, giving L(L+1)/2 predictions
